role: Fold-level orchestration that sits between the CV splitters and the models, built to make leakage structurally difficult. Every step runs inside the fold that owns it: `feature_selection.py` does Boruta-style TreeSHAP shadow selection, keeping only features whose mean absolute SHAP beats a threshold set by permuted shadow copies of themselves, and `norm.py` fits per-symbol z-score normalisers from training rows alone so one symbol's vol regime cannot contaminate another's scaling.

`fold_cache.py` content-addresses expensive LSTM and TCN training: a deterministic fingerprint over config, horizon, fold number, train and test date hashes, and base-model predictions decides whether a fold can be skipped, so nothing retrains by accident and a change to any input invalidates exactly the right cache entries. `conditional_duan.py` then upgrades the global Duan log-to-level bias correction to a per-sample one, training a lightweight XGBoost variance model on OOS residuals from strictly prior folds, or reading squared VVIX as a direct uncertainty proxy.
reads: Fold splits from the CV splitters in utils/cv.py, plus the feature matrices, log-RV targets, and base-model predictions produced upstream by the data, features, and models packages.
feeds: Leakage-controlled inputs into `models` and bias-corrected predictions into `evaluation`, where the tournament ranks everything by QLIKE.

key_files.purpose: The fingerprint-keyed cache that skips retraining sequence-model folds when config, dates, and base-model predictions are all unchanged.
The per-sample walk-forward Duan correction, estimated from prior folds' OOS residuals or a calibrated VVIX proxy.
Boruta-style TreeSHAP selection inside each fold, keeping only features that beat their own shuffled shadows.
Five docstring lines that scope the package: CLI entry points moved to volforecast.cli and only orchestration lives here.

cite.quote:
"""Apply conditional Duan correction using walk-forward variance estimation.

    For each fold k, trains a variance model on squared OOS residuals from
    folds 1..k-1, then predicts σ²(x) for fold k's test samples and applies:

        pred_corrected = pred_original + σ²_hat(x) / 2

    This redistributes the correction across samples based on estimated
    conditional variance: high-uncertainty days get more, calm days get less.
focus: high-uncertainty days get more, calm days get less
